title: 4. Council of Chalcedon (451)
about: Truly God and truly man: one Person in two natures.

items.text: Eutyches, an abbot in Constantinople, taught that after the union Christ's humanity was swallowed up in His divinity, so that He had only one nature. A council at Ephesus in 449, later called the 'Robber Council', backed him. The Emperor Marcian and Empress Pulcheria called a new council at Chalcedon.
Christ weeps as man and raises Lazarus as God. He grows in wisdom, and He is tempted in all things as we are, yet without sin.
St Leo of Rome's letter to Flavian (Letter 28, the 'Tome') was read at the council, and the bishops cried 'Peter has spoken through Leo! Cyril taught the same!'

items.father: St Leo the Great, Letters (Letter 28, the Tome)

items.text: The council confessed one and the same Christ 'in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation'. It also gave 30 canons, among them canon 28 on the honour of Constantinople.

items.father: The definition and canons of the Council of Chalcedon

items.text: Because Christ's humanity is whole and real, everything human except sin is healed in Him: our body, mind, will and feelings. Note: the Coptic, Ethiopian, Armenian and Syriac churches did not accept Chalcedon; dialogue with them continues today.
